title: Russell Brand found guilty of one rape and three sexual assaults at London trial
seoTitle: Russell Brand verdict: guilty on four counts
dek: A jury at Southwark Crown Court convicted the British comedian on four counts on 5 November and cleared him on three others. He is in custody and is due to be sentenced on Monday.
happened: On 5 November a jury at Southwark Crown Court in London found Russell Brand, 51, guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault, against four women, between 2005 and 2009. He was found not guilty of two other counts of rape and one count of attempted indecent assault. Six women gave evidence, and the charges covered 1999 to 2009. Brand had pleaded not guilty to every count. The case followed a 2023 television documentary and press reports, after which women contacted police.

sides.says: Prosecutors described Brand as a "ruthless" sexual predator; senior prosecutor David Roberts called his behaviour "predatory". Detective Superintendent Andy Furphy of the Metropolitan Police said Brand "used his influence, status and fame to exploit and sexually offend against women".
He denied all the charges, saying the encounters were consensual or the allegations made up. His lawyer, Ian Winter, asked for bail to be renewed so he could say goodbye to his children.
Judge Joel Bennathan refused bail, citing Brand's "considerable resources" and a fear he might not attend sentencing, and said he faces a "significant custodial term".

next: Sentencing is due on Monday 9 November. The maximum sentence for rape in the UK is life imprisonment. The women who brought the case are entitled to anonymity under UK law and are not identified here.
summary: British comedian Russell Brand was convicted at Southwark Crown Court on 5 November of one rape and three sexual assaults against four women between 2005 and 2009, and acquitted of two other rape charges and one of attempted indecent assault. Brand denied all the charges. Police say he used his fame to offend against women. The judge refused bail and said he faces a significant prison term. He is due to be sentenced on Monday 9 November.
